newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Sasol pulls staff out of Congo.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Sasol pulls staff out of Congo.

text.p: South African oil and chemicals company Sasol Ltd said on Monday it had evacuated its staff from Congo because of the violence there.
"Our four staff who were there have left the country and are now in Abidjan," a company official told Reuters.
The four would return to South Africa from Ivory Coast on scheduled flights.
"We're just glad that they're safe and out," she added.
Subsidiary Sasol Petroleum International holds a 13 percent interest in Djambala field some 55 km off the Congo coast.
Agip Recherches Congo SA, a unit of Italy's Agip, holds a 52 percent share operates the field. The remaining 35 percent is controlled by the national oil company Hydro Congo.
Development of the Djambala field began in mid-1996. Production was scheduled to start in August next year, with an initial output of 4,000 bpd of high quality crude.

Earlier on Monday the Pretoria government said it had asked the United States and France to help in evacuating South African citizens from Congo because of the ongoing fighting between government forces and militias.
It was not clear how many South Africans were still in the capital after the withdrawal of the Sasol four.
